subject: biology
title: Fertilisation in flowering plants and germination
key_idea: After pollination a pollen tube grows to the ovule and the pollen nucleus fuses with a nucleus in the ovule. This is fertilisation. The ovule becomes a seed, which germinates when it has water, oxygen and a suitable temperature.

blocks.text: (Supplement) Pollen can reach a stigma from the same plant or from a different plant. The two methods have different effects on a population.

items.meaning: The transfer of pollen grains from the anther of a flower to the stigma of the same flower or a different flower on the same plant.
The transfer of pollen grains from the anther of a flower to the stigma of a flower on a different plant of the same species.

rows: Less variation, as only one plant's genes are used
More variation, as genes from two plants are mixed
Response to a change in the environment
Less able to adapt. A new disease or change may kill many plants.
More likely that some offspring survive the change
Little or none, so it works if pollinators are scarce or the plant is isolated
Needs wind or insects, so pollen is wasted and more energy is used making it
Higher chance of fertilisation. Keeps useful varieties unchanged. More chance of inherited disease.
Needs more than one plant of the species nearby

items: Self-pollination uses one plant. Cross-pollination uses two plants of the same species.
Cross-pollination gives more variation, so a population adapts better to change.
Self-pollination is more reliable but gives less variation.

blocks.text: Once a pollen grain lands on a stigma, it grows a tube down to the ovule. Fertilisation is the fusion of the pollen nucleus with a nucleus in the ovule.

diagram.alt: A sequencing activity. Six events are put in order, from a pollen grain landing on the stigma to the zygote forming after the pollen nucleus fuses with the nucleus in the ovule.
diagram.prompt: Put these events in order, from pollination to fertilisation.
steps: A pollen grain lands on the stigma.
The pollen grain grows a pollen tube.
The tube grows down through the style, releasing enzymes.
The tube reaches the ovary and enters the ovule through the micropyle.
The pollen nucleus travels down the tube into the ovule.
The pollen nucleus fuses with the nucleus in the ovule. This is fertilisation.

items: The pollen tube carries the male nucleus to the ovule. The style tissue supplies sugars and water for the tube to grow.
The ovule then becomes a **seed** and the ovary becomes a **fruit**.
The pollen tube grows from the stigma through the style to the ovule.
Fertilisation is the fusion of the pollen nucleus with a nucleus in the ovule.
After fertilisation the ovule becomes a seed and the ovary becomes a fruit.

blocks.text: Germination is the start of growth of a seed into a seedling. A seed will not germinate unless its conditions are right.

rows: It makes the seed swell and lets enzymes work. Enzymes then break down the food stores.
It is needed for aerobic respiration, which releases energy for growth.
Enzymes work best at a warm temperature. If it is too cold they work slowly, and if it is too hot they are denatured.

items: Light is not needed for most seeds to germinate. The seed has its own food store.
The seed stores food such as starch. Enzymes such as amylase digest the starch into sugars.
The sugars are used in respiration to release energy until the seedling can photosynthesise.

items.text: Put equal numbers of seeds on damp cotton wool in separate tubes.
Leave out water, or use boiled water with a layer of oil to remove oxygen, or place a tube in a fridge, and keep a control with all three.
Use the same type and number of seeds, and keep the other two conditions the same in every tube.
Count how many seeds have germinated in each tube after a set time.

items: Seeds need water, oxygen and a suitable temperature to germinate.
Enzymes digest the seed's food stores, and the energy is used until the seedling can photosynthesise.

checks.a: The transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of a flower on a different plant of the same species.

checks.q: Explain the role of the pollen tube.
checks.a: It grows down the style into the ovary and ovule. It carries the pollen (male) nucleus to the ovule so that it can fuse with the female nucleus in fertilisation.

checks.q: State three conditions a seed needs to germinate.
checks.a: Water, oxygen and a suitable temperature.

worked_example.question: Outline the advantages and disadvantages of self-pollination compared with cross-pollination.
answer_points: Advantage: a greater chance of successful pollination and fertilisation.
Advantage: less pollen is wasted, and there is less or no need for pollinators.
Advantage: pollination can still occur in plants that become isolated.
Disadvantage: a limited ability to adapt to a change in the environment, and more chance of inherited disease.
Disadvantage: fewer individuals survive a new infectious disease.
worked_example.tip: Any four score one mark each. Give at least one advantage and one disadvantage.

worked_example.question:
After a pollen grain lands on the stigma of a flower, a pollen tube grows.

Explain the role of the pollen tube.
answer_points: The tube grows down the style.
The tube enters the ovary and the ovule, through the micropyle.
It transports the pollen nucleus (male gamete) to the ovule.
This allows fertilisation, where the male nucleus fuses with the egg nucleus.
worked_example.tip: Any three score one mark each. Say where the tube goes and what it carries.
